Thanks for pointing to getChassisContainedBy(). I can see the pattern — use getAssociatedSubTreePaths, then call object_path(p).filename() to get the name and build the Redfish URL directly.

  In the chassis case, filename() (e.g. HGX_Chassis) is used as-is for the Id and URL, since Redfish Id is just a string with no format constraint.

For PCIeFunction, if we follow the same approach, the URL would become /PCIeDevices/GPU_SXM_1/PCIeFunctions/Function0 instead of /PCIeDevices/GPU_SXM_1/PCIeFunctions/0. 
The Redfish spec doesn't require the URL segment to be a number — only FunctionId (a separate integer property) needs to carry the actual PCIe function number, which we can still extract from the filename.

Would you prefer to go with this approach (use filename() directly as the Id), or keep the numeric-only URL (which requires extracting trailing digits from the filename)?

The numeric URL (/PCIeFunctions/0) was a requirement of the old interface, where properties were named Function0FunctionType, Function1FunctionType, etc. — the number in the URL was needed to construct the correct property name to look up.

Since I'm now switching to the new xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.PCIeFunction interface (one object per function), there's no longer a need to carry a numeric ID in the URL. So I'd like to follow the same pattern as getChassisContainedBy() and use the object path filename directly as the Redfish Id (e.g. /PCIeFunctions/Function0).

The Redfish spec only requires Id to be a unique string — it doesn't need to be numeric. The integer FunctionId property can still be populated separately by extracting the trailing digits from the filename.

Thanks for pushing on this. I did an org-wide search across all openbmc repositories.

peci-pcie is the only repo that still uses the deprecated Function0* properties on Item.PCIeDevice. It dynamically sets properties like Function0VendorId, Function0DeviceId, Function0FunctionType, Function0DeviceClass, etc. via a loop over function numbers 0–7, and has no Item.PCIeFunction support. It was last updated in July 2025.

All other repos (dbus-sensors, pldm, entity-manager, smbios-mdr, phosphor-inventory-manager) either use only the non-deprecated properties (GenerationInUse, LanesInUse) or have no PCIe function inventory at all.

So if this patch removes the old Function0* code path, Intel machines using peci-pcie would lose PCIeFunction data in Redfish.

How would you like to proceed?

Alternatively, I could add backward compatibility: first search for Item.PCIeFunction objects (new interface); if none are found, fall back to iterating Function0\*–Function7\* properties on Item.PCIeDevice (old interface) and emit a warning log. This avoids needing to coordinate with a peci-pcie change. Would that be acceptable?

Yes, you are correct. To populate the PCIeFunctionCollection, you need to establish an association between the PCIeDevice object path and the Function* paths.

In my implementation, for example, the Function0 has an association pointing back to the device:
```
$ busctl get-property xyz.openbmc_project.GpuSensor \
  /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/GPU_0_0/Function0 \
  xyz.openbmc_project.Association.Definitions Associations

a(sss) 1 "exposed_by" "exposing" "/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/GPU_0_0"
```
You should add an association (exposed_by/exposing) under your Function* paths to link them to the S0B0D0 parent device path. This will allow bmcweb to correctly discover and list the members in the collection
